newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close limit down on sell stops.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close limit down on sell stops.

text.p: CME lumber futures crashed the $10.00 per tbf limit late after the September expiration as scattered selling and fund liquidation found little buying interest and sell stops were touched off, traders said.
November fell the limit to close at $361.00 per tbf with about 300 contracts to sell left unfilled. January also ended limit down at $350.00 and other months finished $7.20 to $1.20 per tbf lower.
Limitless September expired earlier at $430.60, up $12.10 on the day. September ranged from unchanged to up $14.80 in thin pre-expiration trade.

Fund liquidation weighed on November starting late morning and prices tumbled when scattered outside selling added to pressure and found little buying interest. Sell stops were touched in November around $368 and increased at $365 which took that month down limit. Other months followed, they said.
November is usually the weak period of the year and lack of buying interest following the runup in September made for a buying void in the market, they added.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $432 per tbf, unchanged from last week.
